To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the detection of uveal melanomas in the UK is not optimal.

(a) the detection and time to treatment (Ttt) of uveal melanomas (UMs) are suboptimal, with a large proportion (40%) of patients presenting late (Ttt >3 months) and with a significant number of UMs being detected by the patient or family (25%), and (b) the Ttt of UM in the UK has not improved since the publication of the first National Guidelines in 2006.

the detection, treatment, and prognosis of uveal melanomas in the United Kingdom.
